question: Should packaged OpenClaw updates officially preserve local `dist` edits and offer opt-in replay, or should modified installed packages remain unsupported?
rationale: The implementation is defensively engineered, but accepting it creates an ongoing support, compatibility, and release-maintenance contract that code review cannot authorize.

options.title: Preserve and opt-in replay
options.body: Adopt recovery-bundle capture by default and allow explicit trusted replay after integrity and topology checks.

options.title: Preserve only
options.body: Capture and report local changes but remove automatic replay, keeping installed-package mutation unsupported.

options.title: Reject modified installs
options.body: Fail updates on modified packaged files and direct users to reinstall or maintain a source checkout.

recommendation.title: Preserve and opt-in replay
recommendation.body: Adopt recovery-bundle capture by default and allow explicit trusted replay after integrity and topology checks.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns much of the update and package-integrity history, is assigned to the PR, and the unresolved question is the supported product contract.
